summary: Backend-only public-endpoint regression completed: 30 tests executed, 18 passed and 12 failed. Core owner login/JWT/me, four-role user creation, duplicate rejection, owner-only user management, password/active updates, self-delete protection, project/location CRUD role rules, assignment duplicate/unassigned-location checks, cashbook empty-receipt/RBAC/autofill/isolation, tagihan lifecycle, team-pay computation, owner-only activities, and core dashboard totals passed. Security controls, two location-isolation paths, receipt validation, missing-resource semantics, audit completeness, and tim dashboard project isolation failed.

critical.issue: Successful login does not set an access_token HttpOnly/Secure cookie, contrary to the requested auth playbook check.
CORS responds Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and does not allow credentials; configured CORS_ORIGINS is ignored instead of using explicit origins with credentials.
No brute-force lockout: after five rejected passwords, the correct password immediately returns 200 rather than 423/429.
A tim user can retrieve assignment data for an unassigned location by supplying location_id (200 with another user's assignment), violating location isolation.
A tim user can retrieve kasbon records from an unassigned location by supplying location_id; expected 403, received 200.
receipt_base64 only receives a truthiness check; malformed value 'not-base64' is accepted and persisted with 200, so a photo receipt is not actually enforced.
Assignment accepts a penagihan user as the target with 200; target user role is not validated as tim.

minor.issue: Deleting an unknown user returns 200 {ok:true} rather than 404.
Updates for unknown IDs return 200 with null instead of 404; matched_count is not checked.
Deletion succeeds but does not create the required activity log entry.
For tim users, jumlah_proyek counts every project (2) while GET /api/projects correctly exposes only the assigned project (1).

action_items: Enforce tim location membership when an explicit location_id is supplied to assignments and kasbon list endpoints.
Validate assignment location/user existence and require the target user's role to be tim.
Decode and validate receipt_base64 as an allowed image/data URL before persisting cashbook entries.
Add failed-login tracking and lockout after five attempts; set a Secure HttpOnly auth cookie if the auth playbook remains required.
Read explicit CORS origins from environment and enable credentialed CORS without wildcard origins.
Check matched_count/deleted_count and return 404 for missing resources; apply consistently to all update/delete endpoints.
Log team-payment deletion and scope tim dashboard project counts to assigned projects.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py list_assignments and list_kasbon overwrite the role-scoped location query with the caller-provided location_id; cashbook already demonstrates the correct explicit membership check pattern.
server.py create_cashbook checks only `if not receipt_base64`; it never base64-decodes, validates MIME type, or confirms image data.
server.py create_assignment never loads/validates the target user or location, allowing non-tim and nonexistent references.
Several update/delete handlers ignore MongoDB matched_count/deleted_count, causing false-success responses and null 200 bodies for missing IDs.
CORS middleware hardcodes wildcard/no credentials and ignores CORS_ORIGINS. Login has no rate-limit/lockout state and returns token JSON only.

The requested /app/auth_testing.md artifact was absent. Source review confirms bcrypt hashes are $2b$ and startup updates the seeded owner's password when it differs, but the seed-password-change path was not destructively runtime-tested.
seed_data_creation: Created isolated TEST_ users/projects/locations/finance records through public APIs; session cleanup removed test records directly from the configured test MongoDB.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run pytest with `-n 0` because the workflow intentionally shares IDs across ordered end-to-end tests; pytest.ini auto-xdist otherwise separates in-memory STATE across workers. Public URL comes from frontend/.env. Final baseline: 30 tests, 18 pass, 12 fail.
rca_of_the_issue: Authorization leaks are query-construction defects: explicit location_id bypasses the computed allowed-location list. Other failures come from missing validation/control branches (base64 decoding, target-role lookup, login lockout/cookie), ignored Mongo write result counts, an omitted delete audit call, and dashboard jumlah_proyek using an unscoped count_documents({}).
